meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. Nobody called me before that zero went into the gradebook, and my son found out on his phone, in the middle of a class. I have until 4:40, Hale, so start with who decided.

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom and a weekend at home are different conditions, Hale. Show me both pages, the September 24 writing and the essay, and I'll read them myself. I'm writing down the date.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. Then the checker's out of it, and I'm writing that down. What does the version history show, with dates and times, and where are those September pages?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology for how Owen found out, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal looped in; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended before your evidence was in front of her.
What moved her: You took the detector off the table and said you were relying on the writing and the version history, which got her to stop arguing about the software and ask for specifics.
What cost ground: You never answered her opening question about who decided, and you never owned entering the zero before anyone called her, which is the point she cares about most.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed well away from that night because you gave no times, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with one sentence owning that the zero went in before you called, then put the September 24 pages and the version history times in front of her so she can check them herself.
